Black Blight.title: Devouring
Black Blight.about:
902 - 1129 AD - Initially recovered from an unmarked vault buried beneath ruins of the original St. Peter's Cathedral in Osnabrück, found in this section of the text is a collection of writings and meditations on the nature of the soul and gnosis. Several hundred years after their unearthing, the contents of this work would go on to influence the beliefs and activities of a breakaway sect of German crusaders during the first crusade. The many atrocities committed by these men, now considered to have been either a part of or a parallel to the Rhineland Massacres, were done in the pursuit of freeing the imprisoned souls of others.
Author(s) unknown, partially translated by C.E. Dobbs & Louis Murtz. (Due to the nature of translating from the all-language, anachronic, anatopic, and language errors may result.)
In loving memory of Gregory J. Shurina, may his eternal soul find peace in the infinite. I'll be thankful for your friendship and our time together forever my dude - you were present in my mind through all of the work I put into this project and I'll greatly miss our lengthy discussions on God, the nature of reality, and all things relating to spirituality & mysticism.
Headphones are recommended - maximum volume yields maximum results; a volume level between 50-80% in headphones is ideal for soundscape visualization.
Experience will be intensified by abuse of consciousness-enhancing substances, late night isolation from social outlets, long walks, deep meditation, constant prayer, and giving glory to The Most High.

trackinfo.title: "From being and its emanations we go thither toward the guiding light of unbeing."
"All our ideas of the self and the ways in which we analyze the self are, to some degree, born out of a desperate yearning for an unachievable simplicity."
"Reality is nothing more than a vague and decaying sense of the various ways in which we have betrayed ourselves."
"We must either choose to live in pursuit of the unattainable ideal (while also accepting the real), or instead assign fractured qualities of the ideal to the eternally unsatisfying real."
"A tomb is a monument to our misguided arrogance, yet an altogether necessary act of screaming one's hopeful penance out into the ether."
"We have manufactured our own failures and will find that God lies waiting motionless within all of them."

Black Blight.title: Gundahar
Black Blight.about:
"We have been attacked.
When at first the enemy forces arrived, no one was sure what was happening; it was still early morning just past daybreak and the men were finishing up their routine training exercises and preparing for their duties.
It started as a low whisper from deep within the forest, rapidly getting louder and louder until ear-piercing shrieks were all around us. They spoke, or rather, screamed in an odd tongue somewhat like that of other known foreigners, but still one not quite distinguishable as any I had ever encountered. Though I had no time for accurate estimation, the magnitude of their unified speech made it seem like they were tens of thousands strong, possibly more.
On the note of their form, however, I must refuse outright to try and recall their twisted appearance for you, lest I might chain both of us to madness permanently. This is all I will say on that matter, and you must trust me that it is in both of our best interests.
What began as a whisper had become a great roar before any man could think to take action. Perhaps I have chosen to forget some of the events, or - as I suspect - something much stranger happened. In any case, before I had time to blink the dead of night was upon us as if time itself had forgotten to play out properly. Most all of the men lay dead and the gatekeeper was struggling to seal the entrance to the keep. It was far too late and all of his efforts proved futile. The barricade had been sabotaged; destroyed completely at some point when no one was looking.
That's when I saw him run out towards them - a lone soldier yelling all the way straight through the indiscernible mass of their horror. As he disappeared into them, his screams gradually became equally terrifying as theirs were. In an instant he was gone completely... devoured by their darkness.
Then, just as quickly as they had come, they were gone - retreating to a slow whisper in the distance and fading to complete silence. I can't for any logical reason explain why their assault ended so abruptly and so strangely, but, as soon as the unknown infantryman had disappeared among their numbers, they turned and left. It was as if these otherworldly abominations had been appeased by receiving an eager participant as opposed to remaining agitated from having to work against us. Speculation and peculiarity aside, I thank The Father for each breath I draw in that man's stead.
The aftermath had left us all quite miserable, to say the very least. With the devastating onslaught finally over, a crack of lightning and the approaching sound of rain brought with them the moonlit view of our fort turned to a battlefield and littered with bodies. The total dead numbered 1762 with 255 either missing, obliterated entirely, or otherwise unaccounted for. 23 of us remain alive. The situation is dismal and this has been a crushing blow to our defenses.
Out of understandable suspicion, those of us left alive and physically capable have searched through everyone's living quarters and found little of interest aside from a journal containing only one entry. The single page had a scribbled drawing of a rocky pit surrounded by trees and a map to its location in the woodlands southwest of the main gate. Accompanying the drawing there was also a great deal of indecipherable text in an unknown language, though there were a few statements we could make out clearly: 'An existence dominated by fear, this is your test. Be wary of those who cannot see the darkness for the light — the road to hell may well be paved with good intention, but the halls themselves are filled with people who would tell you it was worth it. Life does a lot to a man, the least concerning of which is change him. The Father himself could not and would not answer my questions; these are human problems that require human solutions. Run through decay.'
We await your orders."
- Gundahar
Dedicated to every being who has lost their life in the fight for survival and moved forward to something more.

Black Blight.title: Towering Black Spires
Black Blight.about:
559 - 901 AD - The first and most immediately punishing encounter with true darkness is endured and futilely suppressed by humankind for some time.
"The clash that would take place within the depths of man's spirit had revealed not only great potential, but also an equally demanding evil bestowed by the inherent nature of correspondence with the godhead. A vessel of both void and creation, man began to learn that he is his own greatest enemy. Time spent in the belly of the beast digests all desire to create and twist forms - enough deprivation of sensory attachment to reveal that the dichotomy between the blinding light and the all-encompassing shadows are not so different in the finality of their inclinations. After all, Satan himself was to be The Father's most beloved; good and evil to be the best of friends, darkness and light - perfect counterparts, ebb and flow - an ideal and exciting opposition. All with a beloved child trapped between to observe the perfection of the dance."
This piece will function best if listened to all the way through in its correct order.

Black Blight.title: Voids or Pronoia
Black Blight.about:
1836 AD - During an expedition into the ancient Kai cave system in southeast Pakistan, William F. Coppersmith, Peter Copeland, and Daniel Moraine make first known contact with the people of the underground city of Aum.
In later recounting his short time spent there, William had this to say of his experience: "The people of Aum are of a strange sort, they communicate with one another solely through song - if you can call it that - and seem to almost exclusively prefer to focus on their work and duties while allotting little to no time for other pleasures or hobbies. This work of theirs, interestingly enough, is seemingly also accomplished with song. With great boom of voice and lilt of tone, having somehow mastered the natural resonance of their cavernous home, they are able to move massive mounds of earth, close and open stone gates, and even redirect the flow of their underground river as they see fit. The structure of their city gives the impression of something akin to an almost temple-like labyrinth, a true marvel of stonework; the main chamber is dotted throughout with massive hollow tubes carved out of the natural rock surfaces which are presumably intended to be sung into with the goal of augmenting and enhancing the effects of the already impressive resonance."
Headphones are recommended - maximum volume yields maximum results.
Experience will be intensified by abuse of consciousness-enhancing substances in an isolated and pitch black environment.
